chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Madini, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from al-Rida, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
White hair on the forehead is a sign of prosperity, and on the two cheeks is generosity, and on the tufts of hair (on the sides/back) is bravery, and on the back of the head is misfortune.

key_terms.الذَّوَائِبُ: Tufts of hair on the sides or back of the head

ai.seo_question: What do different locations of white hair signify in Shia prophetic traditions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* reflects the Shia tradition of interpreting physical signs as indicators of inner character, linking specific hair locations to virtues like generosity and bravery. It underscores the holistic view in Imami scholarship where bodily features are not merely aesthetic but carry spiritual and ethical significance, often cited to validate the noble traits of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-76 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abi Ayoob Al-Madini, on the authority of Suleiman al-Ja’fari, on the authority of Al-Ridha (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

White hair on the forehead is a sign of prosperity. White hair on the two cheeks is a sign of generosity. White hair on the head is a sign of bravery and white hair on the back of the head is a sign of misfortune.”
